name: movie_betaaur_isi_orbit
label: Movie: beta Aurigae with the three ISI trucks at 650 nm, three nights on a 30 m triangle and four on a 60 m one: the orbital parallax against Hipparcos and the 2026 CHARA orbit, and the twins' diameters free of the distance
notes: The 1.03 and 0.96 mas twins null at 158 and 170 m at 650 nm and the pair's fringe period lambda/a is 41 m at quadrature (a = 3.29 mas): the trucks in a 30 m equilateral triangle (projected 16-30 m, disk |V|^2 0.88) and then a 60 m one (31-60 m, disk |V|^2 0.58) sit inside the first lobe at three position angles 60 deg apart and sweep a full fringe every night, |V|^2 running from ~0 to 0.9. Dec +45: 10.5 h per night above 30 deg at Palomar, twice Spica's window, which repays the factor two in flux.

Seven nights from phase 0.2 (hbtsim's phase 0 is maximum separation; the eclipses fall at 0.25 and 0.75) cover 1.77 of the 3.96 d orbit. The partial eclipses (i = 76.8, a cos i = 0.75 mas against R1 + R2 = 1.00 mas) last 6 h and cover 13 % of the orbit; 38-52 % of the blocks on four of the seven nights fall within hbtsim's near-eclipse margin, are rendered through the two-disk image grid (the movie draws them) and are dropped from the separation fit.

fit_theta_range makes the diameters a free factor k on both catalog radii (their ratio and the SED fixed): the fringe phase pins the orbit's scale s (a and, with the spectroscopic a in AU, the distance), the disk envelope pins s x k, and the two sides of the triangle give the lever -- after the three 30 m nights sigma(theta)/theta is 10 %, after the first 60 m night 3.9 %, after seven 2.6 % (Fisher), while sigma(a)/a stays 0.71 % (0.68 % with the diameters held). The global chi^2 over (scale, node, k) of the seed-7 run is one island from night 2 and ends at a = 3.351 mas (68 % 3.311-3.384; truth 3.292), d = 24.4 pc (24.2-24.7), k = 0.960 (0.915-1.010): theta = 1.009 / 0.939 mas against 1.033 / 0.960 (the 68 % extents are the joint Delta chi^2 < 3.53 region, 1.9 x the marginal sigma).

Kepler's law with the Southworth et al. 2007 masses gives 3.29 mas at the Hipparcos 24.87 pc; the 2026 CHARA orbit found 3.365 mas at 24.30 pc (2.3 % apart): the week decides between them. Not modelled: the eclipse blocks, where |V|^2 encodes the limb-darkened overlap, are not fitted; the two diameters share one factor (a 1 mas twin pair cannot separate them at this S/N).
